scope: Phase-three first batch: workspace view navigation, provider replacement, Help and application Event Log. SDK and viewport implementation unchanged.
status: First batch complete. Phase three remains in progress; completed_phase stays 2.
implemented: Window names, focus, navigation, instance creation/closure and provider replacement are owned by EditorWorkspace. Built-in Help, log, menus, shortcuts and standalone modules share registered commands and view descriptors.

Provider replacement prepares all instances and restores versioned values before switching. Capture/create/restore failure retains existing views, configuration and navigation; old instance scopes expire only on success.
Creation, state and version callbacks cannot submit modifications or edit interactions. A document edit cannot perform direct workspace navigation. Empty documents may still open view windows.

Help is a normal single-instance view. Closing/reopening retains window placement, history, visited links, search and HTML reading positions across reflow. The old dedicated host member, draw branch, display flags and help event variant are removed.

EventLog owns published entries and a bounded worker queue. Queries expose immutable values and UTF-8-safe paged text, including messages larger than 1 MiB. Clear consumes preceding queued messages, and error versions survive repeats and trimming.

Versioned queries reuse their published projection independently of the document version. Built-in status rendering borrows that same result; value-returning and C sink calls retain owned-copy behavior. Closing a view releases its scoped query cache.
Workspace-only Help, log and input views remain usable while native work is active. Unmigrated native document views keep their existing suspension.

regressions: Independent C/C++ public header sizes, callback layouts and absence of STL/SDK/SDL dependencies.
Single and multiple instances, instance targeting, unknown arguments/IDs, wrong threads, failed and throwing navigation, closed scopes and empty-document opening.
Callback mutation refusal, failed captures, native-reference rejection, incompatible state versions, creation/restore failure and failure after an earlier staged replacement.
Real standalone-module log replacement, preserved placement/size, shared log clear, focus and unchanged document/selection/undo state.
Real self-contained help archive through HelpBook/HTML/ImGui, reading-position close/reopen, keyboard remapping, search and workspace interaction during a held native worker.
UTF-8 log messages over 1 MiB, immutable prior copies, versioned cache reuse, failed versions, wrong threads, repeated errors, bounded worker input and clear/trim.
Existing document failure protection, exports, direct NMO opening, SDK object behavior differential and GPU fast-path tests in the complete suite.

Code inspection identified per-frame summary construction/copying, which was replaced with provider-version cache reuse. The final unchanged source and binary passed their first paired capture and following same-program control. Earlier timing differences alone are not assigned solely to query cost.
